segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: Hello can I come in?

segments.speaker: FEMALE LECTURER
segments.en: Oh yes, come in. How can I help you?

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: I was looking for the Economics office. I’ve been all over the Arts Faculty building looking for it but I could only find the School of Accounting and Economic History. Is this the right place?

segments.speaker: FEMALE LECTURER
segments.en: Yes this is the School of Economics.

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: Oh good. Um, I’m a new student and I was wondering if someone could give me some information.

segments.speaker: FEMALE LECTURER
segments.en: Well I might be able to help. I lecture on that program. What do you need to Know?

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: Quite a few things, actually. Firstly, how many lectures a week do I have to Attend?

segments.speaker: FEMALE LECTURER
segments.en: Ah, well, the Economics I course is a double unit so there are two lectures a week and one tutorial. The lectures are scheduled for Tuesday and Thursday.

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: What time?

segments.speaker: FEMALE LECTURER
segments.en: Let me see … You know this information is all in the handout which you should have received yesterday at the orientation meeting.

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: Oh, was there a meeting yesterday? I didn’t know about that … no one mentioned …

segments.speaker: FEMALE LECTURER
segments.en: Yes, there was, but never mind. Now lectures are at four m the afternoon.

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: Four’s a bit late. I’ve got a part time job that starts at four thirty.

segments.speaker: FEMALE LECTURER
segments.en: Well, you can’t be in two places at once, can you, and attendance at lectures is necessary. We expect at least 90% attendance at this university you know.

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: 90%! That’s high. Do they enforce that rule?

segments.speaker: FEMALE LECTURER
segments.en: Yes, we do. We’re pretty strict about it actually.

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: And what times have been set down for the tutorials — do you have that Information?

segments.speaker: FEMALE LECTURER
segments.en: That’s a very well attended course so there’s a number of tutorial times. Monday, Wednesday and Friday, all at 9 o’clock. Yours will be allocated at the first lecture.

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: Can’t I choose the time?

segments.speaker: FEMALE LECTURER
segments.en: Maybe, maybe not.. You’ll have to talk to the lecturer on the course. Dr. Roberts is his name.

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: Oh, OK.

segments.speaker: FEMALE LECTURER
segments.en: Anything else I can help you with while you’re here?

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: Well, yes, actually. Do you know what the course requirements are? I mean, how much work is expected for this course?

segments.speaker: FEMALE LECTURER
segments.en: Well, you have to complete a tutorial paper.

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: What does that involve?

segments.speaker: FEMALE LECTURER
segments.en: Well, it’s a piece of work on a given topic based on some set reading texts. You’ll have to give a small talk to your tutorial group ...

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: How long does that have to be?

segments.speaker: FEMALE LECTURER
segments.en: Oh, about 25 minutes usually.

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: I have to talk for 25 minutes?

segments.speaker: FEMALE LECTURER
segments.en: Yes, that’s right. And then you have to write up your piece of work and give it to the lecturer to be marked.

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: Right. And is that all?

segments.speaker: FEMALE LECTURER
segments.en: No. You also have to complete a 3,000 word essay on a topic.

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: Can I choose the topic?

segments.speaker: FEMALE LECTURER
segments.en: Yes, usually you can.

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: Right. That shouldn’t be too bad.

segments.speaker: FEMALE LECTURER
segments.en: And in addition to that there is an exam.

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: An exam! What sort of exam?

segments.speaker: FEMALE LECTURER
segments.en: Well, it’s an open book exam.

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: Does that mean I can have the text book with me during the exam?

segments.speaker: FEMALE LECTURER
segments.en: Yes, that’s right.

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: And can you give me any idea about the content of the first year of Economics so that I can get into some reading?

segments.speaker: FEMALE LECTURER
segments.en: Well, you’ll be getting the reading list next week when lectures start. All the books are in the library.

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: Yes, but won’t everyone else take them out as soon as they get the reading list too?

segments.speaker: FEMALE LECTURER
segments.en: Well, yes, they might. But most of the important ones are held in Closed Reserve ... that’s a part of the library where you can go to read books but you can’t take them out of the building.

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: What did you call that section of the library?

segments.speaker: FEMALE LECTURER
segments.en: Closed Reserve. However, we do recommend that you buy the core books. You’ll find them useful and you’ll need them for the exam.

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: Yes, I suppose I will. But what is the focus of the course?

segments.speaker: FEMALE LECTURER
segments.en: Well, the course at this university has a vocational focus, that is a focus on preparing its graduates for work, so we’re orientated very much towards employment.

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: So my chances of getting a job are good?

segments.speaker: FEMALE LECTURER
segments.en: Well, provided you get good results.

segments.speaker: MALE STUDENT
segments.en: Well look thanks for your time. You’ve been really helpful.

segments.speaker: FEMALE LECTURER
segments.en: That’s fine. See you next week then.
